title: Efim Liberman's research on cytoskeletal learning

tellings.quote: liberman two friends of mine denil and David liberman their father knew uh hamov and or I think knew Penrose rather and was uh really interested in cytoskeletal learning

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with the writer Eric Wargo, passes on a story about a Soviet scientist named Efim Liberman, the father of two of Michels's friends, Daniil and David Liberman. According to Michels, in roughly the 1970s and 80s Liberman was very interested in "cytoskeletal learning", the idea that learning happens inside the tiny scaffolding within each cell, the cytoskeleton, and he knew or was linked to the researchers Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff, who later took up related ideas. If true, it would mean the brain's thinking runs on something deeper than the connections between nerve cells.
